title: 04. OOP: SOLID Principles (Mastery Level)
summary: SOLID is 5 design principles that make code maintainable, extensible, and testable. They were defined by Robert C.

sections.title: WHAT IS SOLID?
sections.body:
SOLID is **5 design principles** that make code **maintainable, extensible, and testable**. They were defined by Robert C. Martin ("Uncle Bob").

```
S — Single Responsibility Principle
O — Open/Closed Principle
L — Liskov Substitution Principle
I — Interface Segregation Principle
D — Dependency Inversion Principle
```

sections.title: S — Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
sections.body:
### 📖 Explanation:
```
"A class should have ONE and only ONE reason to change."

ONE class = ONE job = ONE responsibility

If your class changes for MORE than one reason → it has too many jobs.
```

### 🧠 Real-World Analogy:
```
A CHEF in a restaurant has ONE job: cook food.
The CASHIER has ONE job: handle payment.
The WAITER has ONE job: serve customers.

If the chef also handles billing AND cleans tables:
→ Any change in billing rules forces changes to the chef class
→ Any change in cleaning policy forces changes to the chef class
→ They're unrelated — chef shouldn't care about them!
```

```python name=srp_complete.py
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  S — Single Responsibility Principle
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ─── ❌ VIOLATION: One class doing 5 jobs ───
class UserManager_WRONG:
    """
    This class has 5 different reasons to change:
    1. User data changes      → change this class
    2. DB schema changes      → change this class
    3. Email template changes → change this class
    4. Password policy changes→ change this class
    5. Report format changes  → change this class
    """

    def __init__(self, user_id, name, email, password):
        self.user_id  = user_id
        self.name     = name
        self.email    = email
        self.password = password

    # Job 1: User data management
    def get_full_name(self):
        return self.name.title()

    # Job 2: Database operations
    def save_to_database(self):
        print(f"  💾 INSERT INTO users VALUES ({self.user_id}, '{self.name}')")

    def fetch_from_database(self, user_id):
        print(f"  💾 SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}")

    # Job 3: Email sending
    def send_welcome_email(self):
        print(f"  📧 Sending welcome email to {self.email}")

    def send_password_reset_email(self):
        print(f"  📧 Sending reset email to {self.email}")

    # Job 4: Password handling
    def validate_password(self, raw_password):
        return len(raw_password) >= 8

    def hash_password(self):
        return f"hashed_{self.password}"

    # Job 5: Report generation
    def generate_user_report(self):
        return f"REPORT: User {self.name} [{self.email}]"

# WHY THIS IS WRONG:
# • Changing email templates requires touching UserManager
# • Adding a new DB column requires touching UserManager
# • Password policy change requires touching UserManager
# • All 3 changes could conflict with each other
# • Testing email requires setting up DB (unnecessary coupling)

print("=" * 55)
print("✅ SRP: One class = One responsibility")
print("=" * 55)

# ─── ✅ CORRECT: Each class has ONE job ───

class User:
    """
    Job: Represent user data.
    Reason to change: User data structure changes.
    """
    def __init__(self, user_id: str, name: str, email: str):
        self.user_id = user_id
        self.name    = name
        self.email   = email

    @property
    def full_name(self):
        return self.name.strip().title()

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"User({self.user_id}, {self.name})"

class UserRepository:
    """
    Job: Persist and retrieve users from database.
    Reason to change: Database or persistence layer changes.
    """
    def __init__(self, db_connection):
        self._db = db_connection

    def save(self, user: User):
        print(f"  💾 DB: Saving user {user.user_id} — {user.name}")
        # self._db.execute("INSERT INTO users ...")

    def find_by_id(self, user_id: str) -> User:
        print(f"  💾 DB: Finding user {user_id}")
        return User(user_id, "Mock User", "mock@test.com")  # simulated

    def find_by_email(self, email: str) -> User:
        print(f"  💾 DB: Finding user by email {email}")
        return User("U001", "Mock User", email)

class UserEmailService:
    """
    Job: Send emails to users.
    Reason to change: Email templates or provider change.
    """
    def __init__(self, email_provider):
        self._provider = email_provider

    def send_welcome(self, user: User):
        subject = f"Welcome to our platform, {user.full_name}!"
        body    = f"Hi {user.full_name}, your account is ready."
        print(f"  📧 Sending welcome to {user.email}: {subject}")

    def send_password_reset(self, user: User, reset_token: str):
        print(f"  📧 Sending reset link to {user.email} (token: {reset_token[:8]}...)")

    def send_order_confirmation(self, user: User, order_id: str):
        print(f"  📧 Order {order_id} confirmed to {user.email}")

class PasswordService:
    """
    Job: Handle password validation and hashing.
    Reason to change: Password policy or hashing algorithm changes.
    """
    MIN_LENGTH    = 8
    REQUIRE_UPPER = True
    REQUIRE_DIGIT = True

    def hash(self, raw_password: str) -> str:
        import hashlib
        return hashlib.sha256(raw_password.encode()).hexdigest()

    def validate(self, raw_password: str) -> list:
        errors = []
        if len(raw_password) < self.MIN_LENGTH:
            errors.append(f"Minimum {self.MIN_LENGTH} characters")
        if self.REQUIRE_UPPER and not any(c.isupper() for c in raw_password):
            errors.append("At least one uppercase letter")
        if self.REQUIRE_DIGIT and not any(c.isdigit() for c in raw_password):
            errors.append("At least one digit")
        return errors

    def is_valid(self, raw_password: str) -> bool:
        return len(self.validate(raw_password)) == 0

class UserReportService:
    """
    Job: Generate user-related reports.
    Reason to change: Report format or content changes.
    """
    def generate_profile_report(self, user: User) -> str:
        return (f"{'='*40}\n"
                f"USER PROFILE REPORT\n"
                f"ID   : {user.user_id}\n"
                f"Name : {user.full_name}\n"
                f"Email: {user.email}\n"
                f"{'='*40}")

# ─── Orchestration: UserService composes the specific services ───
class UserService:
    """
    Job: Coordinate user-related operations.
    Delegates actual work to specialized services.
    """
    def __init__(self, repository: UserRepository,
                 email_service: UserEmailService,
                 password_service: PasswordService):
        self._repo     = repository
        self._email    = email_service
        self._password = password_service

    def register_user(self, user_id: str, name: str,
                      email: str, raw_password: str) -> User:
        # Validate password (password service's job)
        errors = self._password.validate(raw_password)
        if errors:
            raise ValueError(f"Password errors: {errors}")

        # Create user
        user = User(user_id, name, email)

        # Save to DB (repository's job)
        self._repo.save(user)

        # Send welcome email (email service's job)
        self._email.send_welcome(user)

        print(f"  ✅ User registered: {user}")
        return user

# ─── Testing SRP ───
mock_db       = object()   # mock DB connection
mock_provider = object()   # mock email provider

repo     = UserRepository(mock_db)
emailer  = UserEmailService(mock_provider)
pwd_svc  = PasswordService()
reporter = UserReportService()
svc      = UserService(repo, emailer, pwd_svc)

user = svc.register_user("U001", "alice johnson", "alice@test.com", "SecurePass1")

print()
print(reporter.generate_profile_report(user))

# Test each service independently — no coupling!
print(f"\nPassword valid  : {pwd_svc.is_valid('SecurePass1')}")
print(f"Password errors : {pwd_svc.validate('weak')}")
```

sections.title: O — Open/Closed Principle (OCP)
sections.body:
### 📖 Explanation:
```
"Software should be OPEN for extension, CLOSED for modification."

OPEN    = You CAN add new behaviour
CLOSED  = WITHOUT changing existing code

The goal: Add features by writing NEW code, not editing OLD code.
Editing old code = risk breaking existing features
```

### 🧠 Real-World Analogy:
```
POWER STRIP ANALOGY:
  A power strip has slots.
  To add more devices: PLUG IN a new device (extension).
  You do NOT cut open the power strip to add wiring (modification).

  Power strip = Your existing class (CLOSED for modification)
  New device  = New class (OPEN for extension — just plug in!)
```

```python name=ocp_complete.py
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  O — Open/Closed Principle
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

# ─── ❌ VIOLATION: Must modify existing code for every new feature ───
class ReportGenerator_WRONG:
    def generate(self, data, report_type):
        if report_type == "pdf":
            print(f"  📄 PDF: {data}")
        elif report_type == "excel":
            print(f"  📊 Excel: {data}")
        elif report_type == "csv":
            print(f"  📋 CSV: {data}")
        # Adding JSON? Must come back and EDIT this method!
        # Adding XML?  Must come back and EDIT this method!
        # Every new format = risk breaking existing formats

# ─── ✅ CORRECT: Extend without modifying ───

class ReportFormat(ABC):
    """CLOSED for modification — this contract never changes"""

    @abstractmethod
    def generate(self, data: dict, title: str) -> str:
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def get_extension(self) -> str:
        pass

class PDFFormat(ReportFormat):
    """New format = new class. Zero changes to existing code."""
    def generate(self, data, title):
        rows = '\n'.join(f"  {k}: {v}" for k, v in data.items())
        return f"[PDF] ══ {title} ══\n{rows}\n[End PDF]"
    def get_extension(self): return ".pdf"

class ExcelFormat(ReportFormat):
    def generate(self, data, title):
        rows = ' | '.join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in data.items())
        return f"[EXCEL] {title}: {rows}"
    def get_extension(self): return ".xlsx"

class CSVFormat(ReportFormat):
    def generate(self, data, title):
        header = ','.join(data.keys())
        values = ','.join(str(v) for v in data.values())
        return f"# {title}\n{header}\n{values}"
    def get_extension(self): return ".csv"

class JSONFormat(ReportFormat):
    """Adding JSON? Just a new class. No existing code touched!"""
    def generate(self, data, title):
        import json
        return json.dumps({"title": title, "data": data}, indent=2)
    def get_extension(self): return ".json"

class XMLFormat(ReportFormat):
    """Adding XML? Same — just a new class!"""
    def generate(self, data, title):
        rows = ''.join(f"<{k}>{v}</{k}>" for k, v in data.items())
        return f"<report><title>{title}</title>{rows}</report>"
    def get_extension(self): return ".xml"

class ReportGenerator:
    """
    CLOSED for modification — never needs to change!
    OPEN for extension — add new formats by creating new ReportFormat subclasses
    """
    def __init__(self, format_: ReportFormat):
        self._format = format_

    def generate(self, data: dict, title: str) -> str:
        report = self._format.generate(data, title)
        filename = f"{title.lower().replace(' ', '_')}{self._format.get_extension()}"
        print(f"  ✅ Generated: {filename}")
        return report

    def set_format(self, format_: ReportFormat):
        """Switch format at runtime — OCP preserved!"""
        self._format = format_

# ─── Testing OCP ───
data  = {"Revenue": "₹1,20,000", "Users": 450, "Growth": "23%"}
title = "Q1 2026 Report"

formats = [PDFFormat(), ExcelFormat(), CSVFormat(), JSONFormat(), XMLFormat()]

print("=== OCP: Adding formats without modifying ReportGenerator ===\n")
for fmt in formats:
    gen    = ReportGenerator(fmt)
    output = gen.generate(data, title)
    print(f"{output}\n{'─'*50}")

# Adding MarkdownFormat tomorrow? ZERO changes to ReportGenerator!
class MarkdownFormat(ReportFormat):
    def generate(self, data, title):
        rows = '\n'.join(f"| **{k}** | {v} |" for k, v in data.items())
        return f"# {title}\n| Key | Value |\n|-----|-------|\n{rows}"
    def get_extension(self): return ".md"

gen = ReportGenerator(MarkdownFormat())
print(gen.generate(data, title))
```

sections.title: L — Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP)
I — Interface Segregation Principle (ISP)
D — Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
sections.body:
### 📖 Explanation:
```
"High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules.
 Both should depend on ABSTRACTIONS."

"Abstractions should not depend on details.
 Details should depend on abstractions."

THINK OF IT AS:
  High-level  = Business logic (the BOSS)
  Low-level   = Implementation details (the WORKER)
  Abstraction = Interface/ABC (the CONTRACT)

❌ WRONG: Boss directly hires specific Worker
✅ RIGHT: Boss hires via JobContract.
          Any Worker fulfilling the contract can work.
          Boss doesn't care WHICH worker — just that contract is met.
```

### 🧠 Real-World Analogy:
```
WALL SOCKET ANALOGY:
  Your laptop (high-level) doesn't plug directly into the power grid (low-level).
  It plugs into a STANDARD SOCKET (abstraction).
  
  You can move from India → UK → USA:
  → Different power grid (low-level changes)
  → Same laptop + appropriate adapter
  → Laptop doesn't change because it depends on ABSTRACTION (socket standard)

  Without DIP: Your laptop is hardwired directly to India's grid.
               Moving to UK = buy new laptop! ❌
```

```python name=dip_complete.py
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  D — Dependency Inversion Principle
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

# ─── ❌ VIOLATION: High-level depends on low-level directly ───
class MySQLDatabase_BAD:
    def query(self, sql):
        print(f"  🐬 MySQL: {sql}")
        return [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}]

class GmailSender_BAD:
    def send(self, to, subject, body):
        print(f"  📧 Gmail SMTP: {subject} → {to}")

class OrderService_BAD:
    """
    ❌ DIRECTLY depends on MySQL and Gmail.
    Changing DB? Must modify OrderService.
    Changing email? Must modify OrderService.
    Testing? Must have MySQL and Gmail running!
    """
    def __init__(self):
        self.db     = MySQLDatabase_BAD()   # hardcoded!
        self.mailer = GmailSender_BAD()     # hardcoded!

    def place_order(self, user_id, product_id, amount):
        orders = self.db.query(f"INSERT INTO orders...")
        self.mailer.send("user@test.com", "Order Confirmed", f"₹{amount}")
        return orders

# ─── ✅ CORRECT: Depend on abstractions ───
print("✅ DIP: Depend on abstractions")

# Step 1: Define abstractions (the contracts)
class Database(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def query(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> list: pass

    @abstractmethod
    def execute(self, sql: str, params: tuple = ()) -> int: pass

class EmailSender(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> bool: pass

class Logger(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def log(self, level: str, message: str) -> None: pass

# Step 2: Low-level modules implement the abstractions
class MySQLDatabase(Database):
    def __init__(self, host, db_name):
        self.host    = host
        self.db_name = db_name

    def query(self, sql, params=()):
        print(f"  🐬 MySQL [{self.host}]: {sql}")
        return [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}]  # simulated

    def execute(self, sql, params=()):
        print(f"  🐬 MySQL execute: {sql}")
        return 1

class PostgreSQLDatabase(Database):
    def __init__(self, dsn):
        self.dsn = dsn

    def query(self, sql, params=()):
        print(f"  🐘 PostgreSQL: {sql}")
        return [{"id": 1, "name": "Alice"}]

    def execute(self, sql, params=()):
        print(f"  🐘 PostgreSQL execute: {sql}")
        return 1

class InMemoryDatabase(Database):
    """For testing — no real DB needed!"""
    def __init__(self):
        self._store = []
        self._last_id = 0

    def query(self, sql, params=()):
        return self._store.copy()

    def execute(self, sql, params=()):
        self._last_id += 1
        return self._last_id

class GmailSender(EmailSender):
    def send(self, to, subject, body):
        print(f"  📧 Gmail: [{subject}] → {to}")
        return True

class SendGridSender(EmailSender):
    def send(self, to, subject, body):
        print(f"  📧 SendGrid: [{subject}] → {to}")
        return True

class MockEmailSender(EmailSender):
    """For testing"""
    def __init__(self):
        self.sent = []
    def send(self, to, subject, body):
        self.sent.append({"to": to, "subject": subject})
        return True

class ConsoleLogger(Logger):
    def log(self, level, message):
        print(f"  📋 [{level.upper()}] {message}")

class SilentLogger(Logger):
    """For testing"""
    def log(self, level, message): pass

# Step 3: High-level module depends ONLY on abstractions
class OrderService:
    """
    ✅ Depends on Database, EmailSender, Logger abstractions.
    NEVER mentions MySQL, Gmail, or Console directly.
    Can work with ANY implementation — even mocks for testing!
    """

    def __init__(self,
                 database    : Database,
                 email_sender: EmailSender,
                 logger      : Logger):
        # Injected dependencies — not created internally!
        self._db     = database
        self._email  = email_sender
        self._logger = logger

    def place_order(self, user_id: str, product_id: str, amount: float) -> dict:
        self._logger.log("info", f"Placing order: user={user_id}, product={product_id}")

        order_id = self._db.execute(
            "INSERT INTO orders VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (user_id, product_id, amount)
        )

        self._email.send(
            f"{user_id}@test.com",
            "Order Confirmed!",
            f"Your order #{order_id} for ₹{amount:,} is confirmed!"
        )

        self._logger.log("info", f"Order {order_id} placed successfully")
        return {"order_id": order_id, "status": "confirmed", "amount": amount}

    def get_orders(self, user_id: str) -> list:
        return self._db.query(
            "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = ?",
            (user_id,)
        )

# ─── Production setup ───
print("\n=== Production (MySQL + Gmail) ===")
prod_service = OrderService(
    database     = MySQLDatabase("prod-server", "orders_db"),
    email_sender = GmailSender(),
    logger       = ConsoleLogger()
)
result = prod_service.place_order("U001", "P001", 75000)
print(f"  Result: {result}")

# ─── Development setup — swap DB! ───
print("\n=== Development (PostgreSQL + SendGrid) ===")
dev_service = OrderService(
    database     = PostgreSQLDatabase("postgresql://dev-server/dev_db"),
    email_sender = SendGridSender(),
    logger       = ConsoleLogger()
)
dev_service.place_order("U002", "P002", 25000)

# ─── Testing — zero real services needed! ───
print("\n=== Testing (InMemory + Mock) ===")
mock_email = MockEmailSender()
test_service = OrderService(
    database     = InMemoryDatabase(),
    email_sender = mock_email,
    logger       = SilentLogger()   # no console noise in tests
)
test_service.place_order("U003", "P003", 5000)
print(f"  Emails sent in test: {len(mock_email.sent)}")
print(f"  ✅ Full test with zero real services!")
```
